chunks: And the Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Aḥmad ibn Mihrān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, who said:

In one year among the years, lightning strikes occurred in Makkah, and many people died because of that. So I entered upon Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, and he said, initiating the matter before I asked him:
"It is proper that, in the case of the drowned person and the one struck down, one should wait three days regarding him; he should not be buried unless an odor comes from him indicating his death."

I said to him: May I be made your ransom, it is as though you are informing me that many people have been buried alive. He said: "Yes, O ʿAlī, many people have indeed been buried alive; they did not die except in their graves."

key_terms.الْمَصْعُوقِ: the one struck down, here referring to one affected by a lightning strike or sudden incapacitating shock
key_terms.رِيحٌ: an odor serving as a sign
key_terms.يُتَرَبَّصَ: that waiting should be observed before proceeding

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about delaying the burial of a drowned or lightning-struck person?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal precaution regarding those who appear to have died by drowning or by a sudden strike: burial should be delayed for three days unless a clear sign of death appears. It highlights the gravity of verifying death before burial and indicates that some people in the past were buried while still alive.
